title: A 200-rule stylesheet vs a 5000-rule one, same page
claim: Antipattern #27 from web-performance-antipatterns-50.md: 'enormous stylesheets (thousands of rules) - every match consults a bigger rule set.' This is the shape every design system eventually reaches: a stylesheet grown by accretion where any one screen uses a small fraction of it. The question is whether the unused 4800 rules cost anything at all once the page is running, or whether the engine's indexing makes them free.
result: NOT CONFIRMED. No reliable difference at any count from growing the stylesheet 25x, from 200 rules to 5000. The extra 4800 rules match nothing on the page and cost nothing to carry, which means cohtml indexes rules by subject rather than walking the sheet per element. Read against selector-universal-vs-class, the two together say something precise: stylesheet SIZE is free, but defeating the index with a non-class subject is not. Grow the design system; do not write rules the engine cannot bucket.
notes: Applicability gate: DIRECT. Rule 1: one variable, the number of rules in the stylesheet. Rule 2: identical DOM - the same tiles carrying the same classes in both variants. The extra 4800 rules in B are never matched by anything on the page, which is the point: they represent a stylesheet larger than the screen needs. Rule 3: identical JS, byte-for-byte. Rule 4: no text, no assets. Rule 5: 300 tiles occupy 1852x1032 inside 1920x1080. Rule 6: the class churn IS the case and replaces the shared damage driver, so every tile is re-matched against the whole sheet every frame - a static page would let the engine resolve once and never consult the sheet again. Rule 7: no randomness. Rule 8: counts 30/100/300 elements against rule counts fixed at 200 and 5000. Rule 9: plain HTML/CSS/JS - literal rules, because runtime CSS-in-JS is prohibited in Gameface. Rule 10: expected axis is Styles. DIFF SIZE EXCEPTION: the diff is 4800 added lines, because the rule count IS the variable. The first 200 rules are byte-identical between variants; B simply continues the same generated sequence. Generated by tools/make-rule-heavy-cases.js.
